chapter: Germany, Buck's death and ideas about life
title: Bob Hope's praise and Bubbles' trophies
summary: Working with Bob Hope changed Hope's view of Negroes, and Bubbles says no one has done what he has, pointing to trophies from Special Service.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: So, I ain't got no one to work with and Buck starts to work with Timmy Rogers and his band. I got a clipping out of the paper and I got another clipping where Buck said that he was planning on doing an act without me before I'd even thought about it.
Well, what happened is, when I go with Bob Hope, man, that did it. Bob Hope himself had to congratulate me from what he thought about negroes to what he found out in me.
Now that's the kind of pace I set for the negro world, man. Now you know I've been through the mill. You understand?

And nobody's gone through that but me. I know that. I ain't worried about that. I'm just thinking about what fields I have covered in my way of doing and I'm so proud of them and so pleased. I got trophies from way back. You see one up on the wall up there. From way back that one up there. And I've got some in the family room back there. And I've got different things I got from Special Service.

Now at this time I am married for the second time. I'm married the second time now and when I come back this first wife has already served a prison term that I knew nothing about until afterwards, after she had gotten prosecuted for it. But I tried to buy it out, but I couldn't buy it out. Judge told me to send her a letter. I went through that.

Then I meet a girl when I go over with Transatlantic Rhythm, I meet a girl -- was that it? No -- no, the wife that I had then is the one I gave up on account of her getting in this trouble. Then I bumped into--
